title: One state of everything, so no count is ever wrong again

chat.text: You asked for one coherent data structure over the sessions store and the module task homes that represents the current state of everything, rock solid, for a UI or a model alike. Tonight the tasks dashboard showed 0 landed today while 27 had landed, because it read a different reader over a different slice of the store. The dashboard is fixed to a seven-day window from the whole store, and an Opus task mastermind is building the one State class with self-checks that fail loudly. Plan: /framework/ai/doc/one-state.md

message.text: Design posted, building now: one class, State (Server/State.mjs), folds every task in both stores (1,752 session logs + 524 module tasks) through Task.js's rules and writes ai/state.json; each task lands in exactly one bucket (landed, in flight, queued, idle, waiting, stopped, stale), and a second, separate count of today's landings must agree or the dashboard turns red with both numbers. Design: Server/doc/state.md. Found on the way: module tasks completed with the item tool were getting the wall clock as their landing time (37 would have counted as "landed today"); State fixes that on input, and the one-line Task.js fix goes to core/Task's inbox.

Landed and live: every task in both stores now sits in exactly one bucket in ai/state.json (2,065 tasks: 1,310 landed, 1 in flight, 275 idle, 37 stopped, 442 started-but-abandoned), and the tasks dashboard reads it. Landed today is 43 (25 session, 18 module; the old dashboard said 26), and the second, separate count says 44. The week before agrees exactly both ways: 52, 19, 18, 66, 71, 0. The one difference is sheet-handoff-proof: it filed a module task, so Task.js refuses its finish line. The dashboard shows that in red until the Task.js fix (now in core/Task's inbox) lands. Design: Server/doc/state.md.

Landed: ai/state.json now holds every task in exactly one bucket (2,065 tasks). Landed today is 43 by the task rules and 44 by a separate walk; the six days before agree exactly. The one difference is sheet-handoff-proof, shown in red on the tasks dashboard until the Task.js fix in core/Task's inbox lands. Design: Server/doc/state.md.

Built and green. One reader, Server/State.mjs, folds every task log in both stores (sessions and module homes, 2,276 files) through the Task class's rules and counts landed-today two independent ways; after three Task rule fixes the two ways agree on the real repo, 46 and 46, and every one of 2,065 tasks sits in exactly one bucket. The tasks dashboard streams from it and turns red the moment the two counts ever differ. Design and numbers: /Server/doc/state.md and /framework/ai/doc/one-state.md.
